import numpy as np

def process_session(file_data):
    # Extract columns
    ids = np.array(file_data['spectrum_id'])
    shifts = np.array(file_data['raman_shift_cm-1'])
    intensities = np.array(file_data['intensity'])
    
    unique_ids = np.unique(ids)
    n_spectra = len(unique_ids)
    print(f"Found {n_spectra} spectra in file.")

    # Identify the axis from one spectrum
    mask_first = (ids == unique_ids[0])
    axis = shifts[mask_first]
    
    # Check axis range to prevent empty masks
    print(f"Axis range: {axis.min():.2f} to {axis.max():.2f}, size={len(axis)}")

    spectra_matrix = []
    for uid in unique_ids:
        spec_mask = (ids == uid)
        # Ensure we only take intensities for the axis shift values 
        # In case there are multiple entries per shift, though usually not.
        spectra_matrix.append(intensities[spec_mask])
    
    spectra_matrix = np.array(spectra_matrix) # (n_spectra, n_points)
    mean_spectrum = np.mean(spectra_matrix, axis=0)
    
    # Find peak near 1001 cm-1
    # Broaden the search window slightly just in case
    mask = (axis >= 950) & (axis <= 1050)
    if not np.any(mask):
        raise ValueError(f"No data found in range [950, 1050]. Axis values are {axis[:5]}...")
    
    window_intensities = mean_spectrum[mask]
    peak_idx_in_window = np.argmax(window_intensities)
    
    actual_indices = np.where(mask)[0]
    best_idx = actual_indices[peak_idx_in_window]
    peak_pos = axis[best_idx]
    
    # Peak intensities for each spectrum at this position
    peak_intensities = spectra_matrix[:, best_idx]
    mean_int = np.mean(peak_intensities)
    std_int = np.std(peak_intensities, ddof=1)
    rsd = (std_int / mean_int) * 100 if mean_int != 0 else 0
    
    return mean_spectrum, peak_pos, rsd
